sections.title: Desk ranking and honesty checks
sections.what: Checks the Desk lists several sports in order of swing, labels each item as a replay and provisional, attaches a story and receipt to each, and states honestly which sports are not modelled or still pending.
sections.why: Protects the trust the Desk depends on by testing ordering and honest labels together.
sections.watch_out: The minimum item count and specific sport names are fixed, so changes in available data will break it.

summary: Browser test of the Desk page, checking the cross-sport list is ranked by swing, every item has a story and sources, and sports without a model say so honestly.
purpose: Confirms the main daily brief is ordered correctly and is honest about data it lacks.
why: The Desk is the app's headline page, and users must be able to trust its ranking and labels.
how: It opens the Desk and checks the heading, that there are at least five items across cricket, football and F1, and that the swing values are sorted biggest first. It checks each item has a story, a source receipt and a historical replay label. It checks the football swing says not modelled, opens a receipt to check it names the source, and confirms the pending section lists basketball and tennis. It also runs an accessibility check.
inputs: The Desk page and its seeded items.
outputs: Pass or fail for ranking, labels, receipts and accessibility.
risks: The test expects specific sports and a minimum number of items, so a data gap will fail it.
debug: Check the data behind the Desk first. If ranking fails, look at the swing values in the page markup order.
